full_judgment:
2. The opposite party Sujjat Ali was an employee of the petitioner the Chittagong Port Authority in the capacity of Security Guard. On 1.4.79 at 14 hours the opposite party, caught red-handed while removing four pieces of new poplin cloth measuring 26 cubits by two other Security Guards Md Younus and Nasir Ahmed in front of a pan shop just outside gate No. 3 of the Port area After a preliminary enquiry he was charge sheeted on 14.4.79 on the said allegation. The opposite party submitted his explanation on 21.4 79 stating that the cloth recovered from him was purchased by him from Reazuddin Bazar and he had kept the same in the pan shop. An enquiry was held by an enquiry committee in course of which witnesses were examined in presence of the opposite party who did not cross-examine the witnesses. The enquiry committee submitted its findings to the Director of Security who accepted the findings of the enquiry committee and found the opposite party guilty of the charge and a second show cause notice dated 6.6.79 was served on the opposite party in form 'B' proposing a penalty of removal. The opposite party submitted his explanation on the second show cause notice on 16.6.79, ultimately the Director of Security found him guilty of misconduct and removed him from service by the impugned order in Form 'C'. The opposite party thereafter preferred an appeal to the Member, Operation of the Chittagong Port Authority which was rejected Thereafter the plaintiff instituted other Suit No. 10 of 1980 challenging the order of removal as illegal malafide and without jurisdiction. The learned Munsif on consideration of the cases of the respective parties and the evidence on record dismissed the suit. The opposite part preferred an appeal and the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong who heard the appeal allowed the appeal and decreed the suit declaring the impugned order of removal as illegal malafide and without jurisdiction. The petitioner the Chittagong Port Authority then moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. This principle is equally applicable in the case of a Civil Court hearing a Civil suit in which the order of removal of a public servant is challenged. Although, an employee of a statutory body is not strictly speaking a public servant the same principle applies and so long as departmental rules have been followed and so long as the rules of natural justice have not been violated the finding of departmental enquiry held by an Enquiry Committee or for the matter of that a domestic tribunal holding a departmental enquiry cannot be reviewed by the Civil Court as if it was sitting in an appeal. I have also gone through the report of the Enquiry Committee and the materials on which the report was based. This report could by no means be attacked as being based on no evidence far less to be based on mere suspicion and to be malafide. The observation of the learned Additional District Judge that the report of the Enquiry Committee is based on mere suspicion is unjustified. I see no difficulty in holding that the impugned order of removal of the opposite party was made by the Director of Security who was admittedly competent to make such order after following the procedure laid down in the departmental rules and after giving the opposite party a reasonable opportunity to defend himself as well as to show cause against the reposed penalty. The next question is whether the opposite party was given a due opportunity to file departmental appeal against the impugned order of the removal. The learned Additional District Judge appears to have been of the view that appeal was filed to the Member, Operation who was the competent authority to hear appeal but it was heard by the Chairman of the Chittagong Port Authority. In this way the opposite party did not get a proper opportunity for his appeal being heard by the appropriate authority. Rule 17(a) of the Chittagong Port Employees (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1964 provides that an appeal shall lie to the Chairman against an order passed by a head of department and in the instant case there is no dispute that the Director of Security is a head of department. It is therefore evident that the Chairman was the appropriate appellate authority. The learned Additional District Judge clearly misdirected himself in taking the that the Member, Operation of the Chittagong Port Authority was the proper appellate Authority and the Chairman was not the appellate authority in relation to the impugned order of removal which was passed by the Director of Security. The learned Additional District Judge has clearly commit-ted an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice. His judgment and decree cannot be sustained. 

 The Rule is accordingly made absolute. The judgment and decree of the learned Additional District Judge passed in Other Appeal No. 109 of 1981 are set aside and those of the learned Munsif passed in Other Suit No. 10 of 1980 are restored.
